item.title: Wales in fight to retain rising female stars
item.description: Wales will face Norway in a two-legged play-off final in December as they attempt to reach the Women's World Cup for the first time [FAW] Wales are facing a fight to hold on to some of their most promising female footballers amid an "increasingly aggressive" battle to secure the international futures of talented youngsters. Wales have already lost rising Manchester United star Layla Drury, the Wrexham-born forward who became the Red Devils' youngest ever female goalscorer in January. Drury, 17, switched allegiances to England earlier this year having previously represented Wales at under-17 level. The loss of Drury, who has already played eight times for United's first team, was a heavy blow for Wales given her potential and the fact that she was part of the Football Association of Wales' (FAW) development system. The concern for the FAW is that further young Welsh talents could be tempted to switch allegiances, with the pull of a potential Lionesses career regarded as significant. "The market for capturing and retaining talent has become increasingly aggressive," FAW chief football officer David Adams told BBC Sport Wales. "We must make every effort to protect our assets and retain our top talent to protect the future success of the women's national teams." Layla Drury became Manchester United Women's youngest goalscorer, aged 16 years and 220 days, when she scored on her senior debut against Burnley in January [Getty Images] Since 2020, the FAW has focused attempts to develop young female player - aged between 11 and 16 - on programmes in north and south Wales. As part of the system, a group of 31 players are involved in three training sessions a week and play games in the FAW's National Academi boys' set-up in order to aid their development. There is a further pool of 50 players who compete in Adran Premier academies and train with the FAW's girls' development set-up twice a week, while Wales-qualified girls at English academies are invited to a school holiday regional programme. The FAW's development programme, which has been awarded Fifa academy status, also focuses on analysis work and strength and conditioning in an attempt to produce future Wales internationals. A high proportion of players involved are either dual-qualified or have multi-national heritage. The fact that many of those players are likely to sign for clubs in England when aged 15 to 16 – with no top-class women's clubs to join in Wales – can be problematic for the FAW. If players are representing English clubs, they are more likely to come to the attention of those working in England's international pathway. The opportunity to play for England is viewed as appealing for some players because they are one of the women's game's heavyweight sides, having won the Women's Euros twice in a row and reached the Women's World Cup final in 2023. item.title: Fishlock out to keep career alive in NWSL play-offs
item.description: Jess Fishlock will retire at the end of the 2026 NWSL season [Getty Images] On Sunday, 1 November, Wales legend Jess Fishlock will take to the pitch for Seattle Reign against Orlando Pride, not knowing whether it will be her final match. Reign, the club Fishlock has called home since 2013, are competing with NC Courage and Denver Summit for the final National Women's Soccer League (NWSL) play-off spot. Beat Orlando, and Seattle - with whom the 39-year-old has won three NWSL Shields - guarantee an eighth play-off berth in Fishlock's 14-season stint in Washington state. NC Courage and Denver Summit boast a higher goal difference than Reign and sit two and three points behind them respectively, but face each other on the final day. "I've been in this league long enough to understand how this works. I think we've had a couple of situations like this before," said Fishlock. "The beauty of it is you just get to focus on football, which is ultimately all we want to do as players. "All I want to do is get this group into another round of play-offs and see what happens after that. There's a lot going on, which is so fun and so exciting." Wales in fight to retain rising female stars Fishlock called an end to her international career in October 2025, having represented Wales 166 times - a record for men and women. She signed a new contract in Seattle a month later, before confirming in April that she would retire at the conclusion of the 2026 NWSL campaign. Fishlock has never won the NWSL play-offs, finishing as runner-up on three separate occasions in 2014, 2015 and, most recently, in 2023. Progression to the eight-team knockout stage would extend her glittering club career, which includes two Champions League titles, and offer the chance to bow out in style. Jess Fishlock was named the NWSL's Most Valuable Player (MVP) in 2021 [Getty Images] Reign will honour the veteran midfielder, with several activities planned around the stadium, including a commemorative photo booth and dedicated merchandise. Several members of Fishlock's family have flown out to the Pacific Northwest so they can be among the expected 16,000-strong crowd at Lumen Field. "I don't think I've had this many family out, ever. It's been a little crazy," Fishlock added. "I'm not used to having little Rugrats running around everywhere, taking all of my spare energy that I need. But it's been great. "I will really be able to enjoy it post-game. I'm focusing on the match itself and [reaching the] playoffs to keep the season going a little bit longer, which would be nice. "I'm extremely grateful and so appreciative of everybody showing out for me. Everything that the Reign has done has been undeniably incredible and beautiful. "But without sounding ungrateful, I am still very much focused on the game itself. I'm sure post everything, it will hit me far harder than I'm allowing it to hit me right now." item.title: Williams heart warning after career ended at 22
item.description: Keelan Williams received two open-heart surgeries in 2025 [Supplied] At just 22 years old, Keelan Williams faced the hardest decision of his life. Stage one heart failure caused him to call an end to his football career. After two open-heart surgeries and two pacemaker implants, the former Liverpool and Burnley academy prospect had exhausted his medical options. Williams was diagnosed with a bicuspid aortic valve - a congenital condition in which the valve has two flaps instead of three - at the age of 15. But seven years later, further complications forced him to quit the sport both he and his older brother, Wales international Neco Williams, had dreamed of playing professionally since childhood. "It's sad and disappointing that I've had to make the decision to retire and step away from playing because of a cardiac condition," Williams told BBC Sport. Groves' journey from heart surgery to Scarlets Heart condition forces Newport O'Brien to retire Williams' football journey started at local side Cefn United, before he joined a Liverpool satellite academy at six and signed terms with the Reds at eight. He remained in Liverpool's academy until 16, when he joined Burnley, all while representing Welsh youth teams up to under-19s level. Spells at then Cymru Premier side Bala Town and Cymru North club Denbigh Town followed before medical advice prompted an early retirement. Although stepping away has left Williams wondering what might have been, the support he has received and his brother's continued success have helped him adjust to life away from football. "It's always a privilege to chase something you've always dreamed of alongside your brother, who has made it now," Williams added. "Neco is doing so well. I think he is the best full-back in the Premier League. That's what keeps me going, really." Williams also highlights the "crazy" love and backing he has received from family and friends, along with the level of support he has had through social media. "It's something that I don't take for granted. I really treasure the support. It would be much more difficult if I didn't have that. "Football is all about setbacks and how you respond. I've had to stop playing completely, which is more extreme, but you have to look at the positives." 'I'm very lucky in many senses' Keelan Williams (right) pictured alongside his older brother Neco Williams (left) [Supplied] It was during a Wales Under-16s camp that his heart condition was first discovered. "Wales thought that they had found a murmur in my heart, so they stopped me from travelling until further check-ups were made," Williams recalled. "They referred me to Broadgreen Hospital [in Liverpool], where they found that I had an aortic bicuspid valve and I had a slight leak in the valve. "They noticed this without me getting any symptoms. item.title: Hansi Flick reveals 'easy' secret to Lamine Yamal substitution as Barcelona crush Alaves
item.description: FC Barcelona v Real Madrid CF - LaLiga EA Sports - Getty Images Sport Lamine Yamal scored twice as Barcelona bounced back from consecutive defeats with a dominant 6-1 victory over Alaves in Liga. Manager Hansi Flick praised his attacking stars after the emphatic response, while also explaining the decision to substitute his teenage sensation late in the game. Barcelona return to winning ways Yamal and Raphinha both scored twice as Barcelona secured an emphatic 6-1 Liga victory over Alaves on Saturday. Fermin Lopez and Anthony Gordon were also on the scoresheet during a dominant performance at Camp Nou. The comprehensive win provided the perfect response for Hansi Flick's side. It came immediately after their impressive 11-game winning streak was halted by back-to-back defeats against Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid . Mariano Diaz managed a late consolation for the visitors, but Barca were already out of sight following a ruthless attacking display. Flick explains Yamal substitution decision Yamal has enjoyed a remarkable workload this season, starting all 18 matches for Barcelona and Spain. However, Flick was finally able to offer the teenager a brief rest, substituting him for the final 20 minutes against Alaves with the game already won. The Barcelona boss explained that the winger's decisive impact made the substitution much smoother. "When you score two goals, it's easier to go out," Flick admitted after taking the forward off for only the fourth time this season. "I spoke with him at half time. For us, that he has the confidence back with the one vs. one situations, more time and minutes in the second half is good, but it also important he has less minutes." Attacking stars deliver perfect response The hosts wasted no time establishing their dominance, with Raphinha opening the scoring early on. Lopez quickly doubled the advantage before Raphinha netted his 17th goal of the campaign to make it 3-0. Yamal then added the fourth before half-time, capping off a superb team move from the edge of the penalty area. He grabbed his second of the game after the interval with a delicate dinked finish that was initially ruled out for offside. Flick was thrilled with the collective effort from his forward line, saying: "For Lamine it was a great game, but it was good to see the level of the attack: Fermin, Rapha. This is what I want to see after these two defeats. How we react, it was good and in the right way." Massive tests await Flick's side Following their emphatic return to form in Liga, Barc must now shift their focus back to European competition. Aston Villa are set to visit Camp Nou for a crucial Champions League clash on Tuesday. The demanding schedule will then continue with a massive top-of-the-table fixture next weekend. Flick's squad will travel to face Atletico Madrid in a highly anticipated league showdown. These two significant fixtures will define the club's momentum heading into the upcoming international break.

item.title: Centre Hawkins determined to make World Cup
item.description: Joe Hawkins is a former Wales Under-20s international [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Wales centre Joe Hawkins says missing the previous World Cup has made him more determined to make the next global tournament in Australia in 12 months. Following his move from Ospreys to Exeter in 2023, Hawkins was deemed ineligible to play for Wales by Welsh rugby's Professional Rugby Board (PRB) because of the 25-cap rule. The rule says players who have fewer than 25 caps are unavailable to play for Wales if they are not involved with a Welsh club. This ruled him out of the 2023 World Cup in France but Hawkins has since returned to the national side after signing for Scarlets. "I have no regrets," said 24-year-old Hawkins. "It would have been nice to have a World Cup under my belt already, but that just makes me even more excited for potentially what's ahead over the next year. "I loved my couple of years in Exeter with the life experience and playing in the Prem, where you can see a lot of the boys are thriving in now." Wales have a minimum of 12 matches before the World Cup, starting with the Nations Championship opener against Japan in Cardiff next Saturday. "It's always in the back of your mind, knowing you're going into a World Cup year," said Hawkins. "You can probably see from performances from other boys in all positions in the squads that in a World Cup year, the intensity probably rises at the clubs. "Boys are playing for positions and knowing that's the carrot at the end of the year. "But if you're not taking care of the here and now you're not going to get that far." Wales head coach Steve Tandy has selected five different starting midfield partnerships in 13 games since taking charge in September 2025. Hawkins and James are the most prolific pair, having been together for seven games which include victory in an uncapped match against Barbarians. Tandy did go back to Ben Thomas and Max Llewellyn for the 43-0 defeat by South Africa in July, but the Scarlets pair have been the preferred option. item.title: 3 questions Cowboys must answer to beat the Cardinals in Week 8
item.description: The Cowboys beat division rival Philadelphia 38-21 to snap a two-game losing streak, and are now headed home to try for their first winning streak of the season. T he trade deadline looms and the team is deciding whether they'll be buying again. The team struggled defensively against mostly Eagles backups, but their offense stepped up with their best rushing game of the season and timely touchdown passes in the red zone. Dallas fans might have different opinions on the Cowboys' biggest rivals, but their biggest nemesis would seem to be the Arizona Cardinals . The team is 1-8 against the Cardinals in their last nine contests, including 0-4 at AT&T Stadium, with four of their last five losses by double digits. Dallas was usually the favorite and considered the more talented team in most of those matchups, but Arizona has had their number. The Cowboys will need to answer some questions to finally get over the hump against a Cardinals team that upset the Los Angeles Rams two weeks ago. Can Dallas continue to score touchdowns? Dallas is seen as possibly the worst defense in the NFL, but when they match up with Arizona, it's the Cardinals who could be. They are last in scoring defense; the Cowboys are 23rd. Total yards allowed: Dallas is 29th compared to 24th for the Cardinals; EPA per play is an advantage for Arizona, 27th to 30th. They are tied at 20th in passing defense, and the Cowboys are the worst in the NFL in rushing defense. The major difference is on the offensive side. Dallas is a top-five scoring unit and top-10 in total yards, while the Cardinals are 26th and 22nd, respectively. Both teams stink defensively and should move the ball on the other, but only one has played offense at a level to expose the other. Dallas ranks third in red-zone touchdown percentage, scoring at 74%, while Arizona ranks last at 43%. Can Dallas continue their run game momentum? Going into their Week 8 breakout game in Philadelphia, they were 31st at 76 yards per game and dead last in attempts. Things improved drastically after the 200-yard rushing performance against the Philadelphia Eagles . That moved them up to 25th in the NFL with 94 yards per game. Cowboys opponents have made it a strategy to keep the ball away from Prescott and wear down the defense, and that’s why the run game is so important. The Cardinals are fourth in time of possession while the Cowboys are 29th. With Dallas’ red zone advantage, if they can control the time of possession and keep their defense off the field, it could be key to a Dallas victory. Can Dallas change their mentality? item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Iowa picked up a monster win over Wisconsin one week after a heartbreaking loss to Minnesota. Iowa Goes As The Offense Does Just Like Every Other Year When it comes to Hawkeye football, you know the defense is going to be strong. They allowed just 13 points in the loss to Minnesota. item.title: Tyrese Maxey admits he is tired of the 76ers having to come back from big deficits
item.description: Tyrese Maxey admits he is tired of the 76ers having to come back from big deficits originally appeared on The Sporting News . They do not want that to become an issue, so they are ready to put that behind them. Tyrese Maxey does not want the 76ers to get complacent after another comeback The 76ers have been one of the most impressive teams this season, as they are actually living up to the hype. With all of the awesome players the 76ers have on the roster, they are ready to win and be healthy. If they can have more comfortable results, they can afford to rest some of their star players. Maxey would love that, as they are building better contuinity for their goals of winning a title. item.title: ‘Was his own worst enemy’- Steve Kerr explains why Yaxel Lendeborg fell in the NBA Draft
item.description: Photo by Godofredo A. Vásquez/Getty Images Steve Kerr has questioned the NBA’s approach to drafting older prospects after explaining why Yaxel Lendeborg fell in the NBA Draft before joining the Golden State Warriors. The Warriors head coach believes teams overlooked the forward because of his age, despite his impressive combination of size and basketball skills. Lendeborg was 24 when he entered the league, making him older than most rookies. Kerr believes that worked against him during the draft process. Steve Kerr questions NBA teams’ treatment of Yaxel Lendeborg Speaking about Lendeborg’s draft position, Kerr highlighted the skills that should have made the forward an attractive prospect. “Once you get him and you go, ‘Wait a second, this guy is 6’10”, 240, and can dribble, pass, and shoot?’ It’s hard to imagine somebody like that, and then you remember that in the NBA, we penalize guys for being 23. He was his own worst enemy. He should’ve just come out four years ago completely unprepared, and then he would’ve been the second pick in the draft.” Kerr’s comments point to a wider issue with how NBA teams assess prospects who spend more time developing in college. While many young players declare after one season, Lendeborg’s age appears to have counted against him despite his physical attributes and ability on the court. The Warriors ultimately benefited from the situation, landing a player Kerr believes has considerable potential. The coach has also explained why he has been comfortable giving Lendeborg opportunities early in his NBA career. “I didn’t have a ton of expectations. I just wanted to coach him and see where he was. He’s obviously very advanced for a rookie, and he should be,” Kerr said. “He’s 24, older than most guys who come into the league. Some guys have a feel, and some guys don’t. Yaxel has a really innate feel for basketball.” That early trust could prove important as Lendeborg continues adapting to the NBA. Kerr has previously taken a more patient approach with young players, with prospects such as Moses Moody and Gui Santos having to work to earn their minutes. However, Lendeborg offers the Warriors a different option at forward, an area where the team believes his skill set can make a difference. With Jimmy Butler expected to miss an extended period through injury, Golden State could need Lendeborg to take on greater responsibility alongside Stephen Curry and Draymond Green. Kerr’s faith in the rookie suggests the Warriors are willing to give him the opportunity to prove that his age should never have been a reason for teams to pass on him. item.title: Golden State Valkyries set ‘Super Bowl era’ record with historic WNBA championship win
item.description: Photo by Heather Diehl/Getty Images The Golden State Valkyries have done something no other American sports franchise has managed after winning their first WNBA championship. Across professional sports in the US, expansion teams are often looked at as franchises who need time to become a serious force in their leagues. Many teams who have been added late have failed to make noticeable impacts for decades. The Golden State Valkyries have shown they do not have to be like that.. After beating the Atlanta Dream 68-63 in Game 7 of the WNBA Finals on Saturday night, the Valkyries secured their first-ever championship. Considering that this is only the second year they have existed as a team, they have officially set a mark no team has managed in the ‘Super Bowl era’ of professional sports in the United States. Golden State Valkyries become the first team to win in just their second year as a franchise In 2025, when the Valkyries joined the WNBA, they acquired most of their roster through the expansion draft. This included players like Veronica Burton and Kayla Thornton. They weren’t satisfied with just what they had despite making the playoffs, adding Gabby Williams and Kiah Stokes in 2026. Their moves and head coach Natalie Nakase’s basketball savvy have resulted in the Valkyries franchise achieving something no other team has managed. “Golden State becomes the fastest expansion team in American pro sports history (Super Bowl era) to win a title,” Underdog reported. The closest any team has been to this record is the 1970-71 Milwaukee Bucks, who won in their third season. So the Valkyries have made outright history. It is hard to imagine any team beating this record anytime soon. The way the WNBA is growing, any new contenders for it are likely to arrive within that league itself. For now, Golden State stands alone and they deserve all the flowers for their incredible achievement. Mackie was suspended for a three-month period having been found guilty of making illegal payments to players, whilst chairman Sinclair Todd and five other directors were banned for two and a half years each. item.title: Lindstrom's late winner helps MSU hockey knock off North Dakota
item.description: The No. 4 Michigan State hockey team faced its toughest test of the young season on Oct. 31, travelling to Austin, Texas to square off with No. 8 North Dakota in the U.S. Hockey Hall of Fame game. Tied 3-3 late in the third, MSU sophomore forward Cayden Lindstrom scored after jamming at a loose puck in front of the UND net, and with an empty net goal to seal it, the Spartans skated away with a 5-3 victory to improve to 5-1 on the year. Cayden Lindstrom with an immediate response to give us back the lead! pic.twitter.com/EkImzj7558 — Michigan State Hockey (@MSU_Hockey) November 1, 2026 "I thought it was a really good hockey game, and this is why we wanted to play it, coming into a tough environment and (UND) did an unbelievable job with the fans and the crowd," MSU coach Adam Nightingale said. This marked Nightingale's 100th win as head coach of the Spartans. MSU opened the scoring less than a minute into the second period, when sophomore forward Anthony Romani fired a shot past UND goalkeeper Caleb Heil on the power play for his sixth goal of the season. Sophomore forward Eric Nilson added to MSU's lead, taking the puck from end to end unassisted before beating Heil for his second tally of the year. item.title: Misery Index: Ohio State fans have reason to panic after stunning loss at USC
item.description: The cruelest part of sports is often not what happens but rather the lament over what might have been. At the start of the season, Ohio State fans could reasonably boast having the best (and most expensive) roster of any team in the country. But all it took was one injury to quarterback Julian Sayin for this season to become a major what-if and expose all the problems that were hiding in plain sight. Though we don't know for sure if Sayin has an opportunity to return after the serious arm injury he suffered a couple weeks ago at Indiana, Ohio State's 30-18 loss at USC is a telling result. With freshman Luke Fahey thrust into the starting quarterback role, Ohio State is nowhere near the same team — and, if we're being honest, not a College Football Playoff team. On one hand, the Buckeyes are 6-2, which puts them in the same bucket as a whole bunch of teams right now in the Big Ten and SEC that could theoretically win out and realize their postseason ambitions. But the eye test tells a different story: Not only did Ohio State's offense struggle for much of the game with Fahey at quarterback, but the defense completely disintegrated against a USC team that hadn't exactly been lighting the world on fire the last few weeks. Just consider the highlight-reel play made by USC freshman tight end Mark Bowman in the third quarter. Trailing 20-9, the Buckeyes are still in the game if they manufacture a stop. Instead, Bowman gets wide open in the middle of the field, hurdles a defender like he's at the Olympics and then evades a couple tackles until he goes out of bounds at the 3-yard line for a 70-yard gain. The playoff is now 12 teams, but Ohio State can't present any evidence of playoff-quality offense so far with Fahey at the controls. item.description: Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson. Over the past few years, Deshaun Watson’s $230 million contract has been a sore subject for Cleveland Browns fans. His issue was that the Browns paid him for the success he enjoyed with the Houston Texans, only to see him fall short of those expectations after arriving in Cleveland. “It’s no disrespect to Deshaun Watson. I want him to be able to get as much money as he possibly can… But with the Browns, your play hasn’t been that exceeding,” Haden said. “He already owes us $180 million because we didn’t get that [level of] play we were expecting from him.” Watson’s 2026 season has given Cleveland some reason to reconsider his future. The quarterback ranks No. 24 with a PFN QB Impact Score of 70.0, completing 136 of 210 passes for 1,482 yards, seven touchdowns and three interceptions. He has also added 215 rushing yards and a touchdown on 48 carries. His late-game play has been especially important, with five fourth-quarter game-winning drives. That turnaround has also changed the conversation around Shedeur Sanders, who was previously viewed as a possible alternative under center. Even so, Haden believes moving on from Watson could free up money for younger players and other roster needs.
